edition_notes: French version published by TIKI Editions (distributed in Canada by Distribution DUDE); original publisher Happy Baobab, © 2019; authors Roberto Fraga & Sébastien Decad. For 3-6 players, ages 8+, about 30 minutes.

items.rule: Give each player a pouch (pochette), a marker (feutre) and an eraser (effaceur).
Shuffle the photo cards and place the deck in the center of the table.
Select the photo covers (cache-photos) by value according to player count: 3 players use 1,2,3; 4 players use 1,2,3,4; 5 players use 1,2,2,3,4; 6 players use 1,2,2,3,3,4.
Sort the selected covers in descending order so the highest value is on top of the pile, and place the pile in the center next to the photo deck.
Write each player's name on the score sheet and set it aside.
A round is played in three steps in order: 1 Trace (Décalquez), 2 Guess (Devinez), 3 Score (Marquez).
Trace step: each player takes a photo from the deck, turns it over and slides it into their pouch without the other players seeing it.
When all players are ready, say '1, 2, 3, Go!' and all players simultaneously trace the outlines of the elements of their photo on the plastic window of the pouch with the marker.
You may not add elements to your drawing that do not appear on your photo.

You may stop tracing at any time; then immediately take the first cover still available from the pile and slide it into the pouch in front of your photo to hide it, so only your drawing remains visible.
Once you have taken a cover you can no longer keep tracing; put your pouch face down in front of you and wait for the others. Stopping earlier gets a higher-value cover.
Guess step: when every player has hidden their photo, the player whose cover has the highest value reveals their drawing.
The other players try to guess what was drawn; each player may give only one answer, aloud.

If a player guesses correctly, reveal the hidden photo by removing the cover; the first player to give the correct answer wins the photo and places it in front of them, and the drawer keeps their cover in front of them with its value visible.
If two players give the correct answer at the same time, the photo goes to the player with the lowest value cover; if still tied, to the player closest to the drawer in clockwise order.
If nobody guesses, the drawer puts their cover face down in the center of the table and nobody wins the photo.
Repeat reveal and guessing in descending order of cover value until every player has revealed their drawing.
Score step: record each player's points on the score sheet, then put the used photos back in the box and repeat the three steps for the next round.
The game ends after 5 rounds with 3 or 4 players, or after 4 rounds with 5 or 6 players.
Each photo won (by correctly guessing another player's drawing) is worth 2 points.
The drawer scores the value shown on their cover if someone guessed their drawing.
If nobody guessed your drawing, you do not score the points on your cover (though you still score 2 per photo you won).
After the final round, the player with the most points wins the game.
The rulebook gives no tie-break for the final scores.
